pairs.subject: client-fetch-cache
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Detail.tsx:112 The detail paints from the list row the user clicked, but the subject-history count is one the row never carried, and until the related read settles it shows a confident 1 (no other acts) instead of unknown. This is the 'borrowed list row renders zero for a count it never carried' failure named by sibling-entry-warmth.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Detail.tsx:112 The borrow itself is done right: Ledger.tsx:97 finds the row by seq, and read.ts:253 is the cold twin for a deep link. But bySubject is not on the row, so it renders as the value 1 while the read is in flight, and again on every reselect.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Ledger.tsx:132 Stream arrivals are coalesced into one event-driven refresh, and the transition keeps the current render painted while the new one renders. Events win over any timer.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/filter.ts:103 One builder derives the identity from the canonical, fixed-order toSearch, leaving out the windowing-only axes. page.tsx:36 keys the mount with it, so older pages of another filter cannot collide.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:12 The server render, the JSONL route and both Server Actions call one set of plain read functions. actions.ts re-parses the page's own search with the same parser.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Ledger.tsx:96 The seq index is a pure derivation keyed by the rows' reference identity, holds one entry, and can always be recomputed.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/feed.ts:34 The live stream's first connect is held back by a fixed 1.5 s timer (feed.ts:145) rather than an idle callback with a timeout fallback. Scheduled work is cancelled on unmount, which is correct, and there is no intent prefetch of related reads.

app/(studio)/ledger/page.tsx:31 Each mount's rows, counts and strip arrive as server-rendered props, so no client-fetched primary data dies with the view. Older pages are dropped on purpose when the filter identity changes.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Ledger.tsx:77 Each after-render read has a single call site. Older pages use a refuse guard; related reads use debounce plus latest-wins (async-race-guards). No two callers share a key.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Detail.tsx:85 The only held answer is matched by exact seq identity. Nothing is keyed on resemblance.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Detail.tsx:53 The related answer is held in component state owned by one reader. No entry has several claimants with different policies.

pairs.registryProposal: prefetch-and-defer's 'defer to idle, not to a timer' does not cover a long-lived stream whose delay exists to get past a test harness's network-idle window. An idle callback would not guarantee clearing that window, so the technique could name this case: either the readiness signal moves (this repo already uses data-ready), or the timer is argued as a test contract.
